definitions.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

definitions.type: Airy group indexed by real time
definitions.definition: S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3) hat f(k).
P0(f)=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
Pnz=I-P0, denoted P in the supplied proof. Fourier projections P_leq(N) and P_gt(N) retain |k|<=N and |k|>N respectively, for N>=0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has Fourier multiplier (i*k)^(-1) at nonzero integer k and zero at k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2 is denoted D^(-2).

definitions.type: quadratic update family for positive timestep
definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)*Pnz[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)*S_tau Pnz[(Dinv f)^2].

definitions.type: cubic update family for positive timestep
definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L2, Htau(f)=(1/3)*Pnz[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv Ftau(f)]+(tau/9)*(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)*[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) Dinv2[(S_(s-tau) Dinv2 Ftau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Brackets mean the value at tau minus the value at zero. All products are spatial products.

For every positive tau, Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f) on mean-zero L2 data. Given such tau, mean-zero u0 in L2 and an integer L>=1, set t_n=n*tau, u^0=u0 and u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) for 0<=n<L; write v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. For the target with T>0, specialize tau=T/L. There is no spatial cutoff.

KdV is u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0. An exact solution on [0,T] with H^gamma data means the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma(Ttor)) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation. This describes the convention and asserts no existence. For such a solution write v(t)=S_(-t)u(t), and M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma).
For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s) ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

definitions.type: averaged cubic trilinear Fourier family, initially on polynomials
definitions.definition: For tau>0, t0 real, and mean-zero polynomial inputs f1,f2,f3, define Remainder_(t0,tau)(f1,f2,f3) to have zero mean and, for k!=0, Fourier coefficient -tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t0*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), where p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p and Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. Its bounded extensions will be proved; R^n_(2,tau) means t0=t_n.
Bop_t(f,g)=S_(-t)*partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic functions and by distributional product for L2 inputs.
Jop_t(f,g)=S_(-t) Pnz[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

For a time interval I=[a,b], Cop_I(f,g,h)=integral_a^b S_(-t) Pnz{Pnz[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. Initially this is defined for smooth inputs; the continuous extensions in the source estimates are meant when used for rough inputs.
pstar=23/14.

For a grid start t_n=n*tau, tau>0, and time-independent mean-zero w, Stage_n(t;w)=(1/2) integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(w,w) ds for t in [t_n,t_n+tau]. The associated bilinear stage has w1,w2 in its two slots.

For smooth mean-zero initial data and tau=T/L>0, on I_n=[t_n,t_(n+1)] put f_n=v^n, F_n(t)=Stage_n(t;f_n), z_n(t)=f_n+F_n(t), C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(f_n,F_n(s)) ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(F_n(s),F_n(s)) ds, W_n=Q_n(t_(n+1))+Remainder_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n), V(t)=f_n+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau, and Y_n(t)=V(t)-z_n(t). Put rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(Y_n,z_n) ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t Bop_s(Y_n,Y_n) ds-(t-t_n)*W_n/tau. Define Rres(0)=0 and concatenate rho_n: Rres(t)=sum_(j<n)rho_j(t_(j+1))+rho_n(t) on I_n. For an exact twisted solution v, set e=v-V, delta_n=||f_n-v(t_n)||_2, q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. V is initially stepwise defined; continuity is a proved assertion. The per-step formulas define a tuple of functions for any prescribed smooth mean-zero step state f_n, step start n*tau and positive tau, independently of whether f_n comes from a full trajectory. In that local use, any comparison state w may replace v(t_n) in delta_n=||f_n-w||_2 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. Full concatenation, V on the whole time interval and e=v-V concern a full numerical trajectory and an exact solution as specified above.

inputs.statement: S_t is an isometry on every H^s and preserves real functions and zero mean; Fourier projections contract these norms. For mean-zero L2 inputs, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||Bop_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||Jop_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2 and ||Jop_t(A,B)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||B||_2, uniformly in t. For arbitrary L2 F,G, ||Dinv Pnz(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2. H^1 embeds continuously into L^infinity and satisfies ||AB||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||B||_(H^1). For time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b Bop_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[Jop_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[Jop_t(f',g)+Jop_t(f,g')]dt. Also Jop is symmetric and integral_I Jop_t(Bop_t(f,g),h)dt=Cop_I(f,g,h). These identities hold piecewise in time and add across adjoining steps with their common endpoints. For every fixed tau>0, Ftau:L2_zero->H^1 and Psi_tau:L2_zero->L2_zero are continuous polynomial maps, preserve reality, and map smooth data to smooth data; all finite iterates are therefore well defined and continuous in L2.

inputs.statement: For the source mean-zero smooth scheme, equivalently Psi after exp(-t partial_x^3)=S_t, and t_j=j*tau_s, write f=exp(t_j partial_x^3)u^j and Fsrc_j(t;f)=(1/2)integral_(t_j)^t Bop_s(f,f)ds, Asrc_j(f)=integral_(t_j)^(t_j+tau_s)Bop_s(f,Fsrc_j(s;f))ds. The source identities imply exactly exp((t_j+tau_s)partial_x^3)u^(j+1)=f+Fsrc_j(t_j+tau_s;f)+Asrc_j(f)-Rsrc_j(f,f,f). Here Rsrc_j has zero output at k=0 and, for k!=0, coefficient -tau_s/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t_j*(k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3))*eta_(tau_s)(3*a*b*(a+b),3*k*c*(a+b))*hat f(a)*hat f(b)*hat f(c). This is the remainder in the source's trilinear definition, and is Remainder_(t_j,tau_s) under the displayed identifications. No convergence estimate is part of this identity.

hypotheses: tau_s>0 and a nonnegative grid index.
The input f is smooth mean-zero and the update is exactly (1.4), without a cutoff.

output.statement: For any smooth real mean-zero datum and integer L>=1, tau=T/L, the scheme iterates are smooth, real and mean-zero. With D023 on each step, v^(n+1)=f_n+F_n(t_(n+1))+C_n(t_(n+1))-Remainder_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n). Hence V(t_n)=v^n and V(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1), so V is continuous and piecewise smooth on [0,T]. Also Y_n'=Bop_t(f_n,F_n)+(1/2)Bop_t(F_n,F_n)-W_n/tau, Y_n(t_n)=0, and Rres is continuous, piecewise smooth with Rres'= -Bop_t(Y_n,z_n)-(1/2)Bop_t(Y_n,Y_n)-W_n/tau; consequently V'=(1/2)Bop_t(V,V)+Rres' on each step and distributionally globally. All V,Y_n,z_n,Rres and W_n are mean-zero.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary smooth real mean-zero datum and integer L>=1. H001 gives tau=T/L>0. N005 ensures all iterates are smooth, real and mean-zero. In E005 set tau_s=tau, t_j=t_n and f=v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. The source exponentials exp(t partial_x^3) are S_(-t), its quadratic stage is F_n, its A^n is C_n(t_(n+1)), and its R_2^n is exactly D014 with t0=t_n: both alpha=3ab(a+b), beta=3kc(a+b), phase and coefficient -tau/(18ik) agree. The source update equals D009–D011 term by term, including its mean term tau/9 and final endpoint term -1/(27tau). Therefore E005 gives the displayed identity for v^(n+1).

In D023 every stage and integral vanishes at t_n. At t_(n+1), Q_n cancels its part in W_n, so F001 gives exactly V(t_(n+1))=v^(n+1); V(t_n)=v^n. Thus adjoining step values agree. Differentiation on a step gives F_n'=(1/2)Bop_t(f_n,f_n), C_n'=Bop_t(f_n,F_n), Q_n'=(1/2)Bop_t(F_n,F_n), so Y_n'=Bop_t(f_n,F_n)+(1/2)Bop_t(F_n,F_n)-W_n/tau and V'=(1/2)Bop_t(z_n,z_n)-W_n/tau. From the definition of Rres and V=z_n+Y_n, subtracting the two cross and square terms yields V'=(1/2)Bop_t(V,V)+Rres'. Each rho_n starts at zero, so Rres concatenates continuously. Every Bop output and Remainder output has zero mean, as do the initial states; hence all claimed mean restrictions hold. Continuity across the finite grid makes the piecewise differential identity global in distributions, with no jumps.

hypothesis_checks: H001 and L>=1 give tau>0; the step index n is nonnegative.
N005 proves smoothness and zero mean of the iterates; the formula comparison in S001 verifies that the update is exactly source (1.4).
